def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-com:
## Definition

**(a) Setting.** Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the spectral theorem. Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space
([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $A$ and $B$ be self-adjoint operators on $H$
with domains $D(A)$ and $D(B)$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). By the spectral
theorem each of them has a unique spectral projection-valued measure on the
Borel sigma-algebra of $\mathbb R$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]); write $E_{A}$
for the spectral projection-valued measure of $A$ and $E_{B}$ for that of $B$.

**(b) Strong spectral commutation.** The operators $A$ and $B$ **strongly
commute**, or are **spectrally compatible**, when their spectral
projection-valued measures commute on every pair of Borel sets:
$$E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)E_{A}(\Lambda)\qquad\text{for all Borel }\Lambda,\Sigma\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
This is the relation that the term "compatible sharp observables" abbreviates
on the physical pages of the category. It is a condition on the two families
of projections, not on a single vector or on a formal difference of operator
products.

**(c) Not to be confused with a commutator identity on a core.** Let $D$ be a
linear subspace of $D(A)\cap D(B)$ with $A D\subseteq D$, $B D\subseteq D$. The
formal identity $ABu-BAu=0$ for every $u\in D$ is a different condition: it
constrains the two products on $D$ only, whereas clause (b) constrains the
spectral projections of $A$ and $B$ on all of $H$. The two conditions coincide
for bounded everywhere-defined self-adjoint operators, but for unbounded
operators neither one implies the other in general; a pair of self-adjoint
extensions of one symmetric operator whose difference is invisible on a dense
core is a standard witness. Clause (b), not the core identity, is the relation
that governs joint sharp outcomes and the vanishing of suitably formed
products; the examples page of the category records a domain-sensitive
counterexample.

**(d) Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) fix a definition and a comparison of
conditions. They assert no physical claim, no joint measurement, no
simultaneous sharp value and no dynamical statement. All further content about
strong spectral commutation used by the category -- the bounded-calculus
consequences, the joint projection-valued measure criterion and the physical
readings -- is established as separate results with their own hypotheses.
lem-nrqm-uncertainty-schrodinger-roberts:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first argument
([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A,B$ be symmetric
densely defined operators on $H$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]]), and let $u\in D(A)\cap D(B)$
with $\|u\|=1$ satisfy in addition $u\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$, that is
$Bu\in D(A)$ and $Au\in D(B)$. Put
$$a:=\langle Au,u\rangle,\qquad b:=\langle Bu,u\rangle,\qquad x:=(A-a)u,\qquad y:=(B-b)u,\qquad \Delta A:=\|x\|,\qquad \Delta B:=\|y\|,$$
and write $\{A,B\}u:=ABu+BAu$ and $[A,B]u:=ABu-BAu$ for the pairings at $u$.
Then:

(a) $a,b\in\mathbb R$, $x,y\in H$, and
$$\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle=\tfrac12\bigl\langle\{(A-a),(B-b)\}u,u\bigr\rangle=\tfrac12\langle\{A,B\}u,u\rangle-ab, \qquad \langle[A,B]u,u\rangle=-2i\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle ;$$

(b) *(Robertson bound)* $\Delta A\,\Delta B\ge\tfrac12\bigl|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle\bigr|$;

(c) *(Schroedinger-Robertson bound)*
$$(\Delta A)^{2}(\Delta B)^{2}\ge\Bigl(\tfrac12\bigl\langle\{(A-a),(B-b)\}u,u\bigr\rangle\Bigr)^{2}+\tfrac14\bigl|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle\bigr|^{2},$$
that is, with the expanded anticommutator pairing
$(\Delta A)^{2}(\Delta B)^{2}\ge\bigl(\tfrac12\langle\{A,B\}u,u\rangle-ab\bigr)^{2}+\tfrac14\bigl|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle\bigr|^{2}$;

(d) equality holds in (c) if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent;
in particular the Robertson bound (b) follows from (c) because the first
square is nonnegative;

(e) if $A$ and $B$ are bounded everywhere-defined self-adjoint operators, then
the product-domain hypothesis $u\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$ holds for every unit
$u\in H$ and clauses (a)-(d) apply to every unit $u$.

No energy-time inequality and no apparatus statement is made.

def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread.physical_scope: The reading of preparation variance and preparation spread for an assigned sharp observable of the framework: the variance and standard deviation of the outcome law of a preparation, their units, their existence hypotheses through the moment theorem, the centered-vector form for pure preparations of domain vectors, and the resulting definition of the product of two spreads. The item fixes terminology and readings of P1 and P2 only; it asserts no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance, no joint measurement, no dynamics and no empirical result, and it does not claim that any preparation has finite moments automatically.

def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread:
## Definition

**(a) Setting.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the
observable and probability postulate P2 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with
declared unit $u_{A}$ and outcome law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ in a preparation
$\rho$, in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).

**(b) Preparation variance.** When the mean
$m(\rho):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and the second
moment $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ of the outcome
law are finite, the **preparation variance** of $(A,u_{A})$ in $\rho$ is
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\rho)\bigr)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda),$$
read in the square $u_{A}^{2}$ of the declared unit, and the **preparation
spread** is $\Delta_{\rho}A:=\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A)^{1/2}\ge0$, read in
the unit $u_{A}$. When either quantity is not finite the variance and the
spread of the pair in $\rho$ are **not defined**; the definition does not
extend them by $+\infty$.

**(c) Values and hypotheses.** The variance and its hypotheses are exactly
those of the moment theorem: for a pure preparation of a unit vector
$\psi\in D(A)$ the spread is $\Delta_{\psi}A=\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\|$,
equal to $\bigl(\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$
when $\psi\in D(A^{2})$; for a preparation $\rho$ the identities and existence
criteria are those of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] and
[[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]]. In particular a mean exists
exactly when $\rho$ is concentrated on the domain of $|A|^{1/2}$ in the sense
of those items, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments
automatically.

**(d) Products of spreads.** For two assigned sharp observables $(A,u_{A})$
and $(B,u_{B})$ in a common preparation $\rho$ in which both spreads are
defined, the product $\Delta_{\rho}A\,\Delta_{\rho}B$ is a nonnegative real
number read in the product unit $u_{A}u_{B}$; for a pure preparation of a unit
vector in $D(A)\cap D(B)$ it is
$\|(A-a)\psi\|\,\|(B-b)\psi\|$ with the real means $a=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $b=\langle B\psi,\psi\rangle$.

**(e) Reading and scope.** The spread $\Delta_{\rho}A$ is a property of the
pair (preparation, assigned observable): it is the standard deviation of the
outcome law that P2 assigns. It is not an apparatus resolution, not a
measurement error and not a disturbance of the preparation; those are further
objects that require a declared instrument or apparatus model and are not
introduced here. Clause (b) makes no claim that a preparation realizes a
specific laboratory state, that a laboratory procedure measures $A$ with
resolution $u_{A}$, or that the spread is observed in any experiment; the
identification of an apparatus with the pair $(A,u_{A})$ is a tested
identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] fixes the units in which the
displays are read.
lem-nrqm-uncertainty-bounded-borel-calcu:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero
complex Hilbert space and let $A,B$ be self-adjoint operators on $H$ with
spectral projection-valued measures $E_{A},E_{B}$ that strongly commute in the
sense of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]] clause (b):
$$E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)E_{A}(\Lambda)\qquad\text{for all Borel }\Lambda,\Sigma\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
For a bounded Borel function $h$ write $h(A):=\int h\,dE_{A}$ and
$h(B):=\int h\,dE_{B}$ for its operators under the bounded Borel functional
calculus ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]). Then:

(a) for all bounded Borel $f,g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$,
$$f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A);$$

(b) for every bounded Borel $f$ one has $f(B)D(A)\subseteq D(A)$, and
$$A\,f(B)x=f(B)Ax\qquad\text{for every }x\in D(A);$$
the same statement holds with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged, and it is
also true with $f(B)$ replaced by any bounded linear combination or norm limit
of bounded Borel functions of $B$;

(c) for every bounded Borel $f$ the bounded operator $f(B)$ commutes with all
spectral projections of $A$: $f(B)E_{A}(\Lambda)=E_{A}(\Lambda)f(B)$ for every
Borel $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R$. Consequently, for real-valued bounded Borel
$f$ the pair $(f(A),B)$ strongly commutes: the map
$F(\Lambda):=E_{A}(f^{-1}(\Lambda))$ is a projection-valued measure on the
Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ representing the bounded self-adjoint operator
$f(A)$, and $F(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)F(\Lambda)$ for all Borel
$\Lambda,\Sigma$; hence also $(f(A),g(B))$ strongly commutes for real-valued
bounded Borel $f,g$.
thm-nrqm-uncertainty-joint-pvm-criterion:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero
complex Hilbert space and let $A,B$ be self-adjoint operators on $H$ with
spectral projection-valued measures $E_{A},E_{B}$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then the following are equivalent:

(i) $A$ and $B$ strongly commute in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]] clause (b), that is
$E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)E_{A}(\Lambda)$ for all Borel
$\Lambda,\Sigma\subseteq\mathbb R$;

(ii) there is a regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel
sigma-algebra of $\mathbb R^{2}$ whose values on measurable rectangles
([[def-measurable-rectangle]]) are
$G(\Lambda\times\Sigma)=E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)$, and whose marginals are
$G(\Lambda\times\mathbb R)=E_{A}(\Lambda)$ and
$G(\mathbb R\times\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)$;

(iii) $f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A)$ for all bounded Borel functions
$f,g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$, where the operators are those of the bounded
Borel functional calculus ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]).

If these conditions hold, the projection-valued measure $G$ of (ii) is unique,
and for all bounded Borel $f,g$ one has the representation
$$f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A)=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}f(a)g(b)\,dG(a,b).$$
lem-nrqm-uncertainty-product-domain-comm:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix integers $d\ge1$,
$r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space with the componentwise position and momentum operators
$Q_{j},P_{k}$ of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clauses (a) and (b), with domains
$$D(Q_{j})=\{f=(f_{l}):\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\},\qquad D(P_{k})=\{f=(f_{l}):\ D_{k}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\},$$
and let $D_{k}$ denote the weak partial derivative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]). Then:

(a) *Product rule.* If $f\in H^{(r)}$ has $x_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
and $x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ (the latter read
componentwise), then $x_{j}f$ lies in $D(P_{j})$ and
$$D_{j}(x_{j}f)=f+x_{j}D_{j}f;$$

(b) *The product domain.* $D(Q_{j}P_{j})=\{f\in D(P_{j}):\ x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\}$
and $D(P_{j}Q_{j})=\{f\in D(Q_{j}):\ D_{j}(x_{j}f)\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\}$,
and their intersection is
$$D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{j}f,\ x_{j}f,\ x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\};$$

(c) *Commutator identity.* For every $f\in D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$,
$$(Q_{j}P_{j}-P_{j}Q_{j})f=i\hbar\,f;$$

(d) *Core.* The componentwise Schwartz class
$\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]])
is contained in $D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$, and (c) holds on it.

No identity of unbounded products is asserted outside $D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$;
in particular no identity is asserted on $D(P_{j})$ alone.
lem-nrqm-uncertainty-approximation-by-pr:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix integers $d\ge1$,
$r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$, and let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
with the componentwise position and momentum operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]. Let
$\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ with $\psi\ne0$ be a class and let
$D_{P}:=D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$ be the product domain characterized in
[[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-product-domain-commutator-identity]] clause (b). Then
there is a sequence $(\varphi_{n})_{n\ge1}\subseteq D_{P}$ with
$$\varphi_{n}\to\frac{\psi}{\|\psi\|},\qquad Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\to\frac{Q_{j}\psi}{\|\psi\|},\qquad P_{j}\varphi_{n}\to\frac{P_{j}\psi}{\|\psi\|},\qquad \|\varphi_{n}\|=1$$
in $H^{(r)}$. In particular, if $\psi$ is a unit vector, then
$\varphi_{n}\to\psi$, $Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\to Q_{j}\psi$ and
$P_{j}\varphi_{n}\to P_{j}\psi$ in norm, and consequently
$$\langle Q_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle\to\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \|Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\|\to\|Q_{j}\psi\|,\qquad \langle P_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle\to\langle P_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \|P_{j}\varphi_{n}\|\to\|P_{j}\psi\| .$$

pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation.physical_scope: Conditional statements about the preparation spreads of two assigned sharp observables of the framework in a pure preparation of a unit vector: the weak Robertson bound Delta A Delta B >= |Im<A psi, B psi>| for unit vectors in both domains, the Robertson bound Delta A Delta B >= |<[A,B]psi,psi>|/2 and its anticommutator refinement when the product domains also contain the vector, and the automatic validity of these hypotheses for bounded observables. The statement is a conditional consequence of P1 and P2 and the cited mathematics; it concerns preparation spreads of outcome laws only, and asserts no apparatus error, no disturbance, no joint measurement, no energy-time inequality and no empirical result.

pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the observable and
probability postulate P2 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ and $(B,u_{B})$ be assigned sharp
observables with outcome laws $\mu^{A},\mu^{B}$ and let
$\Delta_{\rho}A,\Delta_{\rho}B$ be their preparation spreads in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]]. Let $\psi$ be a unit vector and
write $a:=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, $b:=\langle B\psi,\psi\rangle$. Then:

(a) **Weak form.** If $\psi\in D(A)\cap D(B)$, then the means $a,b$ are real,
the spreads $\Delta_{\psi}A$ and $\Delta_{\psi}B$ are defined, both are read in
the units $u_{A}$ and $u_{B}$, and
$$\Delta_{\psi}A\,\Delta_{\psi}B\ge\bigl|\operatorname{Im}\langle A\psi,B\psi\rangle\bigr| .$$

(b) **Robertson form.** If in addition $\psi\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$, that is
$B\psi\in D(A)$ and $A\psi\in D(B)$, then the pairing
$\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle:=\langle AB\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle BA\psi,\psi\rangle$
is defined, is purely imaginary, and
$$\Delta_{\psi}A\,\Delta_{\psi}B\ge\tfrac12\bigl|\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle\bigr| ,$$
read in the product unit $u_{A}u_{B}$; moreover the anticommutator refinement
$$(\Delta_{\psi}A)^{2}(\Delta_{\psi}B)^{2}\ge\Bigl(\tfrac12\bigl\langle\{(A-a),(B-b)\}\psi,\psi\bigr\rangle\Bigr)^{2}+\tfrac14\bigl|\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle\bigr|^{2}$$
holds, with equality in the refined bound if and only if $(A-a)\psi$ and
$(B-b)\psi$ are linearly dependent.

(c) **Bounded observables.** If $A$ and $B$ are bounded everywhere-defined
self-adjoint operators, then clauses (a) and (b) hold for every unit
$\psi\in H$ with all hypotheses automatic ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).

(d) **Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1
and P2 and the cited mathematics. They concern the spreads of the two outcome
laws in one preparation; they introduce no joint outcome law, no apparatus
resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance of the preparation, and no
time observable. In particular no energy-time inequality is asserted, and
clauses (a)-(c) do not claim that a laboratory procedure realizes either
observable or attains the bounds; whether a concrete preparation and apparatus
realize the pair $(A,u_{A})$ and produce the spread $\Delta_{\psi}A$ is a
tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.

pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-position-momentum-.physical_scope: The position-momentum preparation relation of the massive spin-s particle model of the framework, for one particle of mass parameter m>0 and spin label s: for every unit state vector in D(Q_j) cap D(P_j) the product of the preparation spreads of the j-th position and j-th momentum is at least hbar/2, with no product-domain hypothesis, together with the equality characterization by linear dependence of the centered vectors and the exact imaginary part -hbar/2. The statement is a conditional consequence of P2, P5 and P6 and the cited mathematics; it concerns the spreads of the two separately assigned outcome laws and asserts no joint outcome law of position and momentum, no apparatus realisation, no disturbance and no empirical result.

pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-position-momentum-:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, and the
internal-factor assignment P6 of the framework, read for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and $r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $Q_{j},P_{j}$ be the model's $j$-th position and
$j$-th momentum operators with their maximal domains, and let
$\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}$ and $\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}$ be their preparation spreads in
the reading of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]]. Let
$\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ be a unit vector and put
$$a:=\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad b:=\langle P_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad x:=(Q_{j}-a)\psi,\qquad y:=(P_{j}-b)\psi .$$
Then:

(a) $\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}$ and $\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}$ are defined and
$$\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}\,\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}\ge\frac{\hbar}{2};$$

(b) if in addition $\psi\in D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$, then
$(Q_{j}P_{j}-P_{j}Q_{j})\psi=i\hbar\psi$ and the bound of (a) follows from the
Robertson relation for the two observables;

(c) for every unit $\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ the centered pairing has the
exact imaginary part
$$\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle=-\frac{\hbar}{2};$$
consequently equality $\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}=\hbar/2$ holds if
and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent and
$\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle=0$;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P5, P6 and the cited
mathematics. It concerns the two separately assigned position and momentum
outcome laws in one preparation, needs no hypothesis on the products
$Q_{j}P_{j}$ or $P_{j}Q_{j}$, and asserts no joint outcome law of position and
momentum (which does not exist; see the compatibility results of this page),
no apparatus realization, no disturbance of the preparation, no dynamics and
no empirical result. Massless, relativistic, singular-potential and boundary
realizations are separate models for which no such relation is asserted.

pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-compatible-sharp-o.physical_scope: The reading of strong spectral commutation as compatibility of assigned sharp observables: the equivalence with the existence and uniqueness of a joint sharp observable, the joint outcome law with its two marginal laws in every preparation, and the conditional statement that in the framework's declared ideal Lueders instrument the finite-resolution joint bins reproduce the joint law with order-independent ideal updates. The statement is a conditional consequence of P1, P2, P3 and the cited mathematics; it asserts no laboratory realization of the joint instrument, no disturbance statement and no empirical result, and the joint law is a mathematical object of the framework, not a measured distribution.

pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-compatible-sharp-o:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the ideal
conditional measurement postulate P3 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ and $(B,u_{B})$ be assigned sharp
observables with spectral projection-valued measures $E_{A},E_{B}$
([[def-projection-valued-measure]],
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]). Call a regular
projection-valued measure $H$ on the Borel sigma-algebra of $\mathbb R^{2}$ a
**joint sharp observable** of the pair when its marginals are the two spectral
measures,
$$H(\Lambda\times\mathbb R)=E_{A}(\Lambda),\qquad H(\mathbb R\times\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)\qquad(\Lambda,\Sigma\ \text{Borel}),$$
and call the pair **compatible** when such an $H$ exists. Then:

(a) **Criterion.** The pair is compatible if and only if $A$ and $B$ strongly
commute in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]] clause (b), if and only if
$f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A)$ for all bounded Borel $f,g$; the joint sharp observable
$H$ is then unique, and for bounded Borel $f,g$
$$f(A)g(B)=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}f(a)g(b)\,dH(a,b) .$$

(b) **Joint outcome law.** If the pair is compatible, then for every
preparation $\rho$ the assignment
$$\mu^{H}_{\rho}(S):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,H(S)\bigr)\qquad(S\subseteq\mathbb R^{2}\ \text{Borel})$$
is a probability measure on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R^{2}$, the **joint
outcome law** of the pair in $\rho$, and its marginals are the individual
laws:
$$\mu^{H}_{\rho}(\Lambda\times\mathbb R)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\Lambda),\qquad \mu^{H}_{\rho}(\mathbb R\times\Sigma)=\mu^{B}_{\rho}(\Sigma) .$$
For the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ it reads
$\mu^{H}_{\psi}(S)=\|H(S)\psi\|^{2}$.

(c) **Ideal finite-resolution joint instrument.** If the pair is compatible
and $(P_{1},\dots,P_{n})$, $(Q_{1},\dots,Q_{m})$ are the projections of two
finite disjoint Borel partitions of $\mathbb R$,
$P_{i}:=E_{A}(\Lambda_{i})$, $Q_{j}:=E_{B}(\Sigma_{j})$ with
$\bigcup_{i}\Lambda_{i}=\bigcup_{j}\Sigma_{j}=\mathbb R$, then
$R_{ij}:=H(\Lambda_{i}\times\Sigma_{j})=P_{i}Q_{j}$ are mutually orthogonal
projections with strong sum $I$, and in the framework's declared ideal sharp
measurement of the family $(R_{ij})$ the outcome probabilities are
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})$ with marginals $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{i})$
and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho Q_{j})$; the sequential declared ideal measurements
of $(P_{i})$ and then $(Q_{j})$ give the same joint law
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})$, with order-independent conditional states,
and both update families are repeatable on the corresponding outcomes.

(d) **Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P3 and
the cited mathematics. A joint sharp observable, when it exists, is a
mathematical object of the framework: it supplies a joint outcome law, not an
apparatus. The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes the joint
measurement, with its resolution, losses and systematics, is a physical
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7. No disturbance statement, no dynamics and no empirical result is asserted.

pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-position-momentum-.physical_scope: The incompatibility of the j-th position and j-th momentum of the massive spin-s particle model: their spectral projection-valued measures do not commute, so the pair possesses no joint sharp observable with the two spectral measures as marginals. The statement is a conditional consequence of P2, P5 and P6 and the cited mathematics; it asserts no approximate joint measurement, no apparatus, no error-disturbance relation and no empirical result, and it concerns the model's assigned sharp observables only.

pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-position-momentum-:
## Statement

Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment P6, read
for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$ and spin label $s$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a coordinate index $j$. Then:

(a) the spectral projection-valued measures $E_{Q_{j}}$ and $E_{P_{j}}$ of the
model's $j$-th position and $j$-th momentum do not strongly commute: there are
Borel sets $\Lambda,\Sigma\subseteq\mathbb R$ with
$E_{Q_{j}}(\Lambda)E_{P_{j}}(\Sigma)\ne E_{P_{j}}(\Sigma)E_{Q_{j}}(\Lambda)$;

(b) consequently the pair $(Q_{j},P_{j})$ is not compatible: there is no regular
projection-valued measure $H$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R^{2}$ whose
marginals are $E_{Q_{j}}$ and $E_{P_{j}}$, and in particular the framework
assigns to the pair no joint sharp outcome law in any preparation;

(c) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, P5, P6 and the cited
mathematics and concerns the model's assigned sharp operators only. It does
not assert that no approximate or unsharp joint measurement exists, gives no
error-disturbance relation, and records no apparatus or empirical result.

rem-nrqm-uncertainty-scope-and-empirical.physical_scope: A scope audit of the uncertainty and compatibility page: it records that the page reads P1 and P2 in the framework's vocabulary, proves conditional inequalities and compatibility criteria for preparation spreads and spectral projection-valued measures, and asserts no apparatus error, disturbance, approximate joint measurement, time-energy relation, joint position-momentum law, dynamics, empirical value or experimental finding. It proves nothing itself and reports no observation.

ex-nrqm-uncertainty-gaussian-minimum-spr.physical_scope: An exact model computation for the spin-0 massive particle model of the framework: the normalized Gaussian preparation, its position and momentum outcome densities, the spreads sigma/sqrt(2) and hbar/(sigma sqrt(2)) and the product hbar/2, and the linear dependence of its centered position and momentum vectors that realizes the equality case of the position-momentum preparation relation. The example uses the model's own sharp outcome laws and the cited mathematics; it computes no dynamics, models no measurement, records no empirical value and claims no characterization of all equality states.

texp-nrqm-uncertainty-spin-half-incompat.physical_scope: The spin-one-half internal factor of the massive particle model: the exact identity for the sum of the three component spreads in every unit state, the resulting lower bound hbar^2/2 and the impossibility of a state with all three component spreads small, the failure of spectral compatibility for every pair of spin components with the explicit projection witness, and the saturation of the Robertson bound in the S_z eigenstates. The statement is a conditional consequence of P1, P2, P5 and P6 and the cited finite-dimensional mathematics; it asserts no measurement, apparatus, dynamics, empirical value or claim about angular momentum in space.

texp-nrqm-uncertainty-spin-half-incompat:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor assignment P6, read for the spin-$\tfrac12$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s=\tfrac12$ and $r=2$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Write
$S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ for the model's internal-factor operators of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (c), so that
$J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$ in the Pauli matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e), and let
$\Delta_{\psi}S_{i}$ be the preparation spread of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]]. Then, for every unit
$\psi\in H_{1/2}$:

(a) with $\langle\mathbf S\rangle_{\psi}:=\bigl(\langle S_{x}\psi,\psi\rangle,\langle S_{y}\psi,\psi\rangle,\langle S_{z}\psi,\psi\rangle\bigr)\in\mathbb R^{3}$,
$$\sum_{i\in\{x,y,z\}}\bigl(\Delta_{\psi}S_{i}\bigr)^{2}=\frac{3\hbar^{2}}{4}-\bigl|\langle\mathbf S\rangle_{\psi}\bigr|^{2}\ge\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2},$$
so at least one component satisfies
$\Delta_{\psi}S_{i}\ge\hbar/\sqrt6$; in particular no unit state has all
three component spreads equal to zero;

(b) for every pair of distinct components the spectral projection-valued
measures fail to commute; explicitly, with
$P_{i}^{\pm}:=\tfrac12(I\pm\sigma_{i})$ the spectral projections of $S_{i}$ at
$\pm\hbar/2$,
$$P_{x}^{+}P_{y}^{+}-P_{y}^{+}P_{x}^{+}=\tfrac{i}{2}\sigma_{z}\ne0,$$
and cyclically; consequently no pair of the three components possesses a joint
sharp observable in the sense of
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-compatible-sharp-observables-and-joint-law]];

(c) in the state $\psi=f\,e_{1/2}$ with any unit spatial factor
$f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and the basis vector
$e_{1/2}$ of the internal factor,
$$\langle S_{z}\rangle_{\psi}=\frac{\hbar}{2},\qquad \langle S_{x}\rangle_{\psi}=\langle S_{y}\rangle_{\psi}=0,\qquad \Delta_{\psi}S_{x}=\Delta_{\psi}S_{y}=\frac{\hbar}{2},\qquad \Delta_{\psi}S_{z}=0,$$
and $\Delta_{\psi}S_{x}\Delta_{\psi}S_{y}=\hbar^{2}/4=\tfrac12|\langle[S_{x},S_{y}]\psi,\psi\rangle|$,
so the Robertson bound of
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]] is attained in this state;

(d) **Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5, P6
and the cited finite-dimensional mathematics. They concern the internal-factor
coupling constants of the model; they assert no laboratory measurement of a
spin component, no Stern-Gerlach apparatus model, no dynamics, no empirical
value and no interpretation of $S_{i}$ as a rotating body or as orbital
angular momentum.

rem-nrqm-uncertainty-energy-time-caveat.physical_scope: A scope and reading remark on energy-time statements in the framework: time is a real parameter of the dynamical evolution and not a self-adjoint observable, so the Robertson relation does not apply to a pair of energy and time; the only relation recorded here is the conditional timescale bound of the graph-domain Ehrenfest theorem, under its stated curve, domain and normalization hypotheses, with the timescale defined from the mean of a chosen observable. No universal time observable, no universal energy-time inequality, no linewidth model and no empirical claim is made.

rem-nrqm-uncertainty-error-disturbance-d.physical_scope: A scope and reading remark separating three notions on the uncertainty and compatibility page and the measurement page of the category: the preparation spread of an outcome law, the resolution or error of a declared apparatus, and the disturbance of the preparation produced by a measurement. The remark records that the framework's postulates define the first through the Born law and the second and third only through declared instruments and apparatus models, and that no universal error-disturbance relation, no universal disturbance bound and no empirical result is asserted. It proves nothing itself.

rem-nrqm-uncertainty-examples-scope-limi.physical_scope: A scope audit of the examples companion of the uncertainty and compatibility pair: it records that the companion contains one exact model computation, one finite internal-factor deduction, one purely mathematical counterexample and two scope remarks; that it contains no experiment, no apparatus realization, no measured value, no trial count and no statistical inference; and that every identification of a preparation or apparatus with the model's objects is a tested identification under P7. It proves nothing itself.
